title: Asahi Kasei Develops Novel Lithium Pre-doping Technology to Raise Energy Density and Lower Cost of Silicon-rich Lithium-ion Batteries - Batteries News
content:
Asahi Kasei Develops Novel Lithium Pre-doping Technology to Raise Energy Density and Lower Cost of Silicon-rich Lithium-ion Batteries
Novel lithium pre-doping technology to raise energy density and lower costEnables the use of low-cost lithium carbonate with existing production linesGlobal PoC evaluations and licensing to accelerate commercialization
BUSINESS WIRE
)–Asahi Kasei, a diversified global company, has developed a novel pre-doping technology for high-voltage lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) with silicon-based anodes. This technology enables lithium carbonate to serve as an additional lithium source at lower voltages, reducing the permanent capacity loss that typically occurs in silicon-rich cells during the first charge–discharge cycle. Going forward, Asahi Kasei will work closely with customers worldwide to explore practical applications of the technology through proof-of-concept (PoC) evaluations.
With the growing adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) and humanoid robots, LIBs are being required to deliver ever-higher energy densities. In response, development efforts have focused on partially replacing graphite with silicon-based materials in the anode and on increasing the operating voltage of cathode materials.
However, silicon-based anodes suffer significant, irreversible capacity loss during the initial charge, severely limiting the battery’s lifespan and total energy density. Compensating for this effect requires greater amounts of cathode active material, which in turn leads to higher material use and higher costs.
Asahi Kasei focused on lithium carbonate, which is relatively inexpensive and has an established track record of use as a lithium-ion battery (LIB) material, as an alternative to existing methods. However, because the decomposition voltage of lithium carbonate is far above the nominal operating voltage range of LIBs, its use for lithium pre-doping applications has tended to be difficult.
The lithium pre-doping technology developed by Asahi Kasei uses special additives in the electrolyte to promote the decomposition of lithium carbonate at typical cell voltages of standard LIBs. This allows lithium carbonate to be pre-added to the cathode as a sacrificial lithium source, which is decomposed during the initial charge to supply lithium. The use of low-cost lithium carbonate substantially improves energy density. Internal tests with an NMC (nickel-manganese-cobalt) cell having an anode of 90% graphite and 10% SiO showed a 10% increase in energy density. Furthermore, this technology improves cycle life at low cost per Wh (watt-hour), can be applied without significant modifications to existing battery manufacturing lines, and is expected to be broadly applicable across a range of cathode and anode material systems.
Asahi Kasei plans to license this technology and offer flexible collaboration frameworks that support a phased approach tailored to each customer’s development stage. This strategy is part of the company’s
medium-term management plan
(MTP), which includes its
Technology-value Business Creation (TBC)
initiative. Through TBC, Asahi Kasei seeks to create value from its extensive intangible assets—such as patents, know-how, data, and algorithms—by providing them in various forms, including licensing. Through this licensing-based business development, the company aims to conclude at least 10 new license agreements during fiscal 2025–2027, with a cumulative profit contribution of ¥10 billion or more by around 2030.

title: Sunwoda joins China's flash charging race with battery system promising 10%-97% in 9 minutes - Batteries News

Sunwoda joins China’s flash charging race with battery system promising 10%-97% in 9 minutes
Electric Vehicle Battery Co Ltd (Sunwoda EVB) has unveiled a 15C smart flash charging battery system and aims for 10,000 megawatt charging stations by the end of 2027, joining China’s intensifying race in ultrafast charging.
The Chinese battery maker announced the plan on September 17. The system debuted at a battery industry conference held September 16-17 in Zaozhuang, Shandong province.
The launch comes as Chinese automakers and battery makers step up their push into flash charging. After
(HKEX: 1211) introduced its second-generation Blade Battery and new flash chargers in March, Hongqi, Dongfeng and
(NYSE: XPEV) announced advances in batteries or ultrafast charging infrastructure.
Data Sunwoda presented at the conference showed that the new battery system can charge from 10% to 70% in 5 minutes and from 10% to 97% in 9 minutes at room temperature. A 1-minute charge can add 100 kilometers of range.
The charging times for both intervals match the room-temperature figures BYD announced when it unveiled its
generation Blade Battery
in March.
At minus 20°C, Sunwoda’s new system takes 15 minutes to charge from 10% to 97%. The company said the system can support a driving range of more than 700 kilometers.
Sunwoda also said the system can meet warranty requirements of 10 years or 300,000 kilometers, with no limit on ultrafast charging sessions for vehicles not used commercially, seeking to address concerns that high-rate charging could shorten battery life.
Beyond charging speed, Sunwoda made smart monitoring a focus of the upgrade. The system integrates smart battery cells 3.0, an energy domain controller and an AI cloud-control platform to improve battery monitoring and early fault detection.
The system can provide warnings for more than 20 types of faults 2 to 10 days in advance, with an accuracy rate of 99.77%, the company said in the statement.
An open ecosystem platform combining solar power, energy storage and flash charging, unveiled alongside the battery system, extends the company’s offering into charging infrastructure.
The platform integrates flash charging EV batteries, energy storage systems, megawatt charging units, high-power liquid-cooled charging terminals and an AI cloud-control platform. It supports vehicles from multiple brands and different partnership models.
Sunwoda expects its flash charging ecosystem to include 10,000 megawatt charging stations by the end of 2027. The statement did not disclose station locations, investment plans, the first vehicle models to use the new battery or a mass-production timetable.
Competition in China’s flash charging market has moved from technology launches to network expansion. BYD announced the completion of its
10,000th flash ch
rging station in China
on August 28, reiterating its target of 20,000 stations by the end of 2026.
Other domestic automakers are also advancing the technology. Test results Hongqi
released in July
showed that a battery jointly developed with China Automotive New Energy Battery Technology (CNET) could charge from 10% to 70% in 3 minutes and 41 seconds at 25°C. The brand did not disclose a mass-production timetable at the time.
Dongfeng
rolled out a prototype
of its independently developed ultrafast charger on July 29. Its peak output of 1,500 kW per charging connector matches that of BYD’s new flash charger unveiled in March.
Xpeng announced on September 15 that its first X-Energy megawatt charging station had
begun operating in Hong Kong
. Jointly built with local charging provider Halo, the station is open to drivers of all vehicle brands.
The station has a peak output of 1 megawatt and is equipped with 400 kWh of energy storage. That figure represents the station’s output capacity; actual vehicle charging power still depends on the vehicle’s battery and charging capabilities.

title: Materials Drive Next-Generation Solutions at Battery Show
content:
Materials
Industry Outlook
Solid-state batteries, sodium batteries are key session topics at the industry's largest show for battery technology and issues.
September 21, 2026
3 Min Read
Attendees at The Battery Show North America in Detroit will have ample opprotunities to learn about the latest advances in materials and battery chemistries.
The Battery Show North America
The upcoming Batttery Show at Huntington Place in Detroit, October 12 through 15, will showcase developments in various battery technologies and issues. As expected, several sessions focus on advances in battery materials as engineers work to develop batteries with greater reliability and energy efficiency.
Here are some sessions attendees should find useful and informative. All the session times are Eastern.
Solid-State Batteries at the Crossroads: Promise vs. Production
https://tbsm26.mapyourshow.com/8_0/sessions/session-details.cfm?scheduleid=159
Tuesday, October 13, 1:00 PM - 1:15 PM, Room 140AB
Despite decades of research and investment, commercialization of solid-state batteries remains a challenge due to technical, economic, and scalability hurdles. This session will critically assess whether we are finally on the cusp of widespread solid-state battery adoption or whether semi-solid electrolytes will take over.
Key discussion points will include innovations in solid electrolytes, ranging from sulfides and polymers to halides, and their impact on conductivity and stability. We will also examine the integration of lithium-metal and silicon anodes, a key enabler for higher energy density, and the challenges related to dendrite formation and manufacturability. The session will also analyze how major industry players, including automakers and battery manufacturers, are investing in SSB technology and whether production costs and supply chain constraints could delay mass deployment.
The session will also explore market readiness, policy frameworks, and investment landscapes that could accelerate or hinder the commercialization of SSBs.
Beyond LFP: Where Does Sodium-Ion Fit in the Future Battery Mix?
https://tbsm26.mapyourshow.com/8_0/sessions/session-details.cfm?scheduleid=110
Tuesday, October 13, 3:50 PM - 4:10 PM Room 140AB
The development of solid-state batteries has largely focused on optimizing isolated material properties, such as electrolyte safety—often narrowly defined by non-flammability—or high ionic conductivity. However, this approach overlooks the coupled nature of electrochemical behaviors, where ion transport, interfacial contact, and electrode reactions collectively determine real-world performance and safety.
A critical misconception lies in equating non-flammable electrolytes with inherently safe batteries. In practice, safety risks are primarily governed by unstable electrode reactions and interfacial degradation, rather than electrolyte flammability alone. These unresolved electrochemical challenges at the cell level propagate into system-level penalties, including increased structural complexity, added weight, and higher manufacturing costs. Material reactivity and process sensitivity further hinder scalability.
In this talk, Vincent Yang of Prologium Technology discusses a Solid-State Battery 2.0 platform that shifts from single-parameter optimization to a chemistry-integrated design framework. By simultaneously stabilizing electrode reactions, enabling robust interfacial transport without external pressure, and simplifying material and process requirements, this approach addresses both performance and safety at their origins.
The Pressure Problem in Solid-State Batteries: Engineering for Performance, Durability & Scale
https://tbsm26.mapyourshow.com/8_0/sessions/session-details.cfm?scheduleid=114
Wednesday, October 14, 4:10 PM - 4:30 PM, Room 140AB
Solid‑state battery systems introduce new challenges for mechanical pressure management compared to traditional pouch and prismatic lithium‑ion cells. Conventional elastomeric pads—commonly used to provide low, compliant counterforce during cell breathing—are designed to compress easily while accommodating long‑term cell expansion from mechanisms such as dendrite formation or gas generation.
However, solid‑state chemistries require substantially higher installation pressures, typically 1–3 MPa at beginning‑of‑life, and they experience greater dimensional changes during cycling. While silicone and polyurethane pad materials can achieve these higher counterforces, they generally must be implemented at significantly increased thickness to absorb the larger expansion profiles, which can create packaging and design constraints.
To address these limitations, Rogers is developing differentiated pressure‑management materials engineered to deliver the required force levels for solid‑state cells while maintaining more conventional pad thicknesses, improving both performance and pack‑level integration. Rogers will discuss these materials in a lightning talk
The Best Electrode Is No Electrode: Anode-Free Sodium Batteries
https://tbsm26.mapyourshow.com/8_0/sessions/session-details.cfm?scheduleid=98
Tuesday, October 13, 3:30 PM - 3:50 PM Room 140AB
This talk, given by a former Tesla engineer who has launched a sodium-ion company, will explore how “innovation by subtraction” can be applied to sodium-ion battery chemistry in an anode-free cell design, resulting in the lowest bill-of-materials available.
Scaling Advanced Materials from R&D to Commercial Production
https://tbsm26.mapyourshow.com/8_0/sessions/session-details.cfm?scheduleid=305
Thursday, October 15, 11:00 AM - 11:30 AM Room 140AB
This session examines the challenges of moving advanced battery materials from laboratory research to reliable, cost-effective commercial production. It will explore scale-up, process control, quality consistency, supply availability, qualification timelines, and manufacturing integration required to bring new materials successfully to market.

Oct 12, 2026 TO Oct 15, 2026

North America's largest advanced battery trade show and conference brings together engineers, business leaders, top companies, and innovative thinkers to discover ground-breaking products and create powerful solutions for the future.

lithium-ion batteries
involves a complex process, including material innovation, advanced cell design, and scalable manufacturing techniques. As global industries increasingly rely on energy storage solutions to drive innovation, companies are investing heavily in R&D to meet growing demand. Here are five key takeaways from
Panasonic Energy
’s launch of its new lithium-ion battery research and development facility in Kadoma, Osaka.
1. Prototyping and development in one place
A major highlight of the announcement is the company’s integration of prototyping and development into a single, unified environment. This approach eliminates inefficiencies in traditional workflows, where design and testing often occur in separate facilities. This unified model is particularly advantageous for industries like robotics, automotive, and consumer electronics, where rapid iteration is critical to staying competitive.

For industries such as AI-driven robotics and autonomous vehicles, where scalability is key, this focus on mass production provides a significant competitive edge.

The company’s growth is reflected in its expanding workforce, which now exceeds 500 employees. Together with the Suminoe Production Development Facility, which focuses on manufacturing technology development, the two sites will form one of Japan’s largest dedicated battery development operations, with a combined workforce of approximately 800 people. At Panasonic Energy, we are committed to developing solutions that support this growth while prioritizing sustainability and efficiency.”

Panasonic Energy is also leveraging digital tools to achieve scalability. From cloud-based platforms to AI-driven analytics, these tools enable the company to optimize operations, improve decision-making, and scale its solutions effectively. Digital tools are particularly valuable in managing supply chains, improving product quality, and reducing inefficiencies. In today’s digital age, such tools are essential for companies aiming to succeed.
As Kazuo Tadanobu, CEO of Panasonic Energy, stated, “The adoption of AI, autonomous technologies, and robotics is driving unprecedented energy demand. At Panasonic Energy, we are committed to developing solutions that support this growth while prioritizing sustainability and efficiency.” By prioritizing R&D, the company is not only meeting current market demands but also anticipating future trends in energy solutions, AI, and robotics. As industries evolve and competition intensifies, organizations that invest in R&D will be better positioned to innovate, adapt, and lead in a rapidly changing technological landscape.

HiTHIUM unveils 4 MWh sodium-ion system with 30-year design life and 20,000-cycle battery, targeting 2027 production.
US firms Peak Energy, Alsym, and DOE's LENS Consortium pursue grid storage focus as China scales broad applications.
China-based battery manufacturers are accelerating sodium-ion battery development with announcements that move the technology closer to commercial deployment. In mid-September 2026, CBAK Energy Technology and HiTHIUM unveiled sodium-ion products and capacity plans that position the alternative chemistry as a complement to lithium-ion batteries in energy storage and select mobility applications.
CBAK Energy: 12 GWh plan with dual-chemistry flexibility
CBAK Energy Technology Limited (NASDAQ: CBAT), a Dalian-based lithium-ion battery manufacturer, reported internal test results for its 32140 NH-7Ah full-tab sodium-ion cell and outlined plans for 12 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of annual sodium-ion production capacity, according to a
September 17 news release
The cylindrical cell uses sodium iron phosphate pyrophosphate (NFPP) cathode material paired with CBAK's full-tab design intended to support high-current operation and heat dissipation. Internal laboratory testing demonstrated performance across a 110°C temperature span, from −40°C to 70°C.
Related:
Battery Breaking-News Headlines
Key performance metrics from CBAK's internal testing include:
Fast charging
: 90% state of charge reached within 15 minutes
High-rate discharge
: Capacity retention above 95% during continuous 15C discharge; pulse discharge capability at 28C
Low-temperature performance
: 87.68% discharge capacity retention at −40°C relative to 25°C baseline
Cycle life
: Projected 10,000 cycles under specified protocols; approximately 3,500 cycles at 70°C under 1C/1C cycling to 80% capacity retention
: High pass rate in internal nail-penetration testing; storage and transportation supported at 0% state of charge
CBAK Energy’s 32140NH-7Ah sodium-ion cell undergoing internal nail-penetration testing. Credit: CPAK Energy
CBAK's sodium-ion program targets energy storage, light electric mobility (two- and three-wheelers), and backup power applications. Customer testing of cell samples is currently underway across residential and portable energy storage systems, electric two- and three-wheelers, specialty vehicles, and backup power applications.
"We view sodium-ion as a complement to lithium-ion, with the strongest potential in applications where power, cycle life, performance across a wide temperature range and supply-chain flexibility must be balanced at the system level," said Dr. Senlin Wang, Head of Sodium-Ion Battery R&D at CBAK Energy.
A distinguishing feature of CBAK's capacity plan is production line compatibility with lithium-ion cell manufacturing, designed to provide flexibility to respond to customer demand for either battery chemistry. The 12 GWh figure represents a conditional planning objective rather than currently installed capacity, with deployment timing dependent on customer qualification and commercial demand.
Related:
Power Up at The Detroit Battery Show 2026
Future development plans include larger cylindrical formats (46- and 60-series cells) for higher-capacity applications and specialized high-rate cells for AI data center backup power applications.
HiTHIUM: Infrastructure-grade system with 30-year design life
HiTHIUM, a Xiamen-based energy storage technology company,
unveiled its next-generation integrated sodium-ion energy storage solution
on September 16, 2026, positioning sodium-ion technology as an infrastructure-grade solution with a 30-year designed service life.
The company's ∞Power N4.0MWh is a 4MWh sodium-ion energy storage system equipped with the ∞Cell N785Ah sodium-ion battery. HiTHIUM announced plans to begin full-scale production and delivery in 2027.
The ∞Cell N785Ah features a 20,000-cycle service life, supports 2 to 8 hours storage durations, and is fully compatible with HiTHIUM's 1,000 Ah lithium-ion manufacturing platform—a design approach intended to support rapid sodium-ion production scale-up.
"We started from the most fundamental chemistry and materials, retracing the 30-year journey of lithium-ion batteries," said Dr. Aileen Wang, Director of Battery Research Institute at HiTHIUM.
Related:
Editors Roundtable: 3 Major News Items in July & August
System-level innovations in the ∞Power N4.0MWh include:
Stacked-cell design
with dedicated battery management system (BMS) featuring state-of-charge (SOC) estimation accuracy of ≤2.5%
Voltage compatibility
: 800–1500V power conversion system (PCS) compatibility, with PCS rated-power utilization rising over 20% compared with HiTHIUM's previous-generation sodium-ion system
Efficiency
: 24-hour comprehensive efficiency exceeding 88%
Thermal management
: Hybrid air-liquid cooling mode with AI-enabled thermal management, reducing operating auxiliary power consumption by 30% and standby auxiliary power consumption by 50%
Footprint
: System architecture optimization reduces station footprint by 30%
"30 years means 10,950 days of validation—a long-term commitment to our customers," stated Dr. Wang. "It means electrochemical energy storage can be viewed, evaluated and held to the service-life standards of infrastructure."
HiTHIUM also launched the ∞Edge Pioneer Program to test batteries and systems in extreme environments, with plans to disclose progress over the next three years and progressively release technology packages targeting a levelized cost of storage (LCOS) of RMB 0.1 per kWh (approximately $0.014 USD).
Context: Sodium-ion vs. lithium-ion
Sodium-ion batteries substitute sodium for lithium as the charge carrier, offering resource abundance, as sodium is widely available and geographically distributed, potentially supporting more diversified sourcing and reduced sensitivity to lithium price volatility; superior low-temperature performance, and safe zero-charge storage and transportation.
The primary trade-off is lower energy density compared to lithium-ion, making sodium-ion better suited for stationary storage and light mobility applications rather than long-range electric vehicles. Both CBAK and HiTHIUM position sodium-ion as complementary to lithium-ion, targeting applications where power density, cycle life, and wide-temperature operation align with system-level requirements.
US sodium-ion initiatives challenge Chinese dominance
While China-based companies have established a leading position in sodium-ion battery development and commercialization, US firms are pursuing distinct strategies with significant recent progress.
Peak Energy and General Motors partnership:
As we reported in June, Peak Energy and General Motors' strategic partnership aims to develop next-generation
sodium-ion battery cells purpose-built for grid storage
. The partnership targets a 20% cost reduction compared to lithium-iron-phosphate systems through passive thermal management, with Peak Energy's planned 4 GWh/year domestic manufacturing facility and GM-co-developed cells targeting commercialization by approximately 2028.
Peak Energy and GM collaborate to develop and deploy next-generation sodium-ion battery cells for BESS. Credit: Maria / Battery TechnologyGuerra
Alsym Energy: As we discussed in July,
Massachusetts-based Alsym Energy is developing
non-flammable sodium-ion batteries that eliminate fire risk entirely
. The company has announced strategic partnerships totaling over 18 GWh, including agreements with ESS Tech, Re:Build, Juniper Energy, and ERITY for deployment across grid-scale storage and mining applications.
LENS Consortium:
The US Department of Energy has funded the LENS (Lithium-free Energy Storage) Consortium, which
focuses on sodium-ion battery chemistries
, providing federal support for fundamental research. LENS aims to develop high-energy, long-lasting sodium-ion batteries using safe, abundant, and cost-effective materials.
US vs. China competitive dynamics
Chinese companies like CBAK and HiTHIUM emphasize compatibility between sodium-ion and lithium-ion production lines, leveraging existing gigafactory infrastructure and vertical integration, while US companies are building dedicated sodium-ion capabilities focused on grid storage and safety-critical applications.
Chinese manufacturers target broad application portfolios with announced capacity plans reaching 12 GWh (CBAK) and full-scale production beginning in 2027 (HiTHIUM), while US efforts concentrate on grid storage and data center applications where passive cooling, non-flammability, and total cost of ownership advantages can offset lower energy density. US developers emphasize supply chain security through abundant domestic materials, safety advantages through non-flammable designs, and system-level economics—positioning sodium-ion as a complement to lithium-ion for applications where these characteristics align with market needs.
Whether US sodium-ion companies can achieve commercial scale comparable to Chinese manufacturers will depend on continued technical validation, manufacturing investment execution, and sustained policy support for alternative battery chemistries.

title: How Maersk is Meeting E-Commerce Delivery Demand
content:
How Maersk is Meeting E-Commerce Delivery Demand
Prioritise Us
on Google
Maersk has agreed to collaborate with Shipstore, a shipping automation platform for high-volume parcel shippers. Credit: Getty Images
Prashant Shah, Head of E-Commerce for North America at Maersk, explains how integrating with Shipstore is reshaping the company's parcel delivery strategy
Maersk has agreed to collaborate with Shipstore, a shipping automation platform for high-volume parcel shippers.
Through the agreement, Maersk's North American e-commerce delivery services are available directly through the Shipstore platform.
The integration is designed to simplify how online businesses manage shipping as they look to meet rising
customer expectations
and expand into new markets.
Prashant Shah, Head of E-Commerce for North America at Maersk, says: “Through our collaboration with Shipstore, we’re making it easier for online businesses to connect with Maersk’s delivery network through a platform they already know and trust. Together, we’re helping customers simplify shipping and deliver a better experience for the people they serve.”
Prashant Shah, Head of E-Commerce for North America at Maersk. Credit: Prashant Shah via LinkedIn
Key Facts: Maersk-Shipstore Integration
Integration connects Maersk's delivery network directly within the Shipstore platform
Businesses can manage Maersk shipping alongside existing carriers in one workflow
Shippers can generate labels, documentation and tracking without switching systems
Deal reflects Maersk's shift beyond ocean freight into last-mile delivery
Positioned as an added option within a multi-carrier strategy
Inside the Maersk-Shipstore integration
Shipstore customers can access Maersk's North American delivery services directly within the platform they already use, rather than logging into a separate system.
Businesses that already run a Maersk
delivery programme
can now execute that volume through Shipstore alongside its existing carriers.
This allows enterprises to generate shipping labels, documentation and tracking information through a single workflow.
Maersk's North American e-commerce operations span inventory management, fulfilment, transportation and final-mile delivery.
The company says it currently handles more than 10 million
e-commerce parcels
annually across the region.
Rather than replacing a shipper's existing carrier relationships, the integration is positioned as an additional option within a multi-carrier setup.
Together, we’re helping customers simplify shipping and deliver a better experience for the people they serve.
Prashant Shah, Head of E-Commerce for North America at Maersk
Why multi-carrier shipping is reshaping e-commerce
The Maersk-Shipstore integration represents a considerable transition across e-commerce logistics, as rising parcel volumes deters companies from relying on a single carrier.
According to Gartner's 2026 Market Guide for Multicarrier Parcel Management Solutions, global parcel delivery volumes are expected to increase by more than a third.
This rise is placing growing pressure on shippers to adapt how they manage delivery capacity across multiple providers.
Gartner’s research also reveals that e-commerce retailers and consumer electronics companies are now spending twice as much managing reverse and returns logistics as they do on outbound orders and deliveries.
Platforms like Shipstore can tackle this increase in volume, as it allows enterprises to manage multiple carriers,
automate workflows
and apply their own business rules to shipments.
For Maersk, the deal also brings a strategic shift as it has historically focused on ocean freight and large container shipping.
It has invested in end-to-end
logistics capabilities
to the final customer, acquiring Pilot Freight Services for US$1.7bn in May 2022 to take ownership over its first, middle, and last-mile B2C home delivery networks in North America.
Key companies
Headquarters: Copenhagen, Denmark
CEO: Vincent Clerc
A global leader in integrated logistics, Maersk operates across 130 countries, connecting ocean freight, port terminals and landside distribution. The company leverages digital platforms, cold-chain logistics and green-fuel fleets to deliver end-to-end supply chain management for global containerised commerce.
ShipStore
Headquarters: Missouri, US
CEO: Jeff Rudd
Shipstore is a multi-carrier shipping platform that automates high-volume, complex logistics across parcel and LTL. The platform connects with hundreds of carriers and technology providers to automate carriers and business systems to automate rate selection, labeling, routing and invoicing.

title: RAVE Aerospace & Arena: Balancing Compliance and Growth
content:
RAVE Aerospace & Arena: Balancing Compliance and Growth
Prioritise Us
on Google
Arena and Rave Aerospace explore how organisations are improving audit efficiency. Credit: Getty Images
In an on-demand webinar, leaders from Arena and Rave Aerospace explore how organisations are building a strong foundation to drive supply chain efficiency
Global supply chains are changing, facing
new pressures
and new obstacles every day.
Leaders are met with instructions to grow with speed, but are also being challenged by increasing compliance needs.
In an on-demand webinar, Marshall Wood, Senior Customer Success Coach at Arena, and Phil Seymour, Director of Engineering Services at RAVE Aerospace, explore how teams are maintaining control over their operations at the same time as meeting growth plans.
Watch the on-demand webinar now
Navigating modern demands
Modern supply chains cannot rely on traditional solutions, as the demands today are at a major high. Businesses are facing greater demand than ever – to do more, to spend less, to cut times – but they are also facing more obstacles.
Around the world, leaders are being challenged by trade relationships, sustainability demands and the integration of technology. With this, there are more risks than ever. Major climate events have become a common occurrence, placing supply chain teams in a constant state of reaction. Alongside this, as technological advancements grow, organisations are seeing an increasing risk of
cyber attack
As a result, teams are working to change the game. Instead of reacting to these events, teams are aiming to get ahead and proactively mitigate any potential risk.
The webinar,
Speed and Compliance: How A&D Teams Keep Control as Programs Scale
, offers insights into how leaders can build a trusted foundation for speed, compliance and growth.
Watch the on-demand webinar now
Marshall Wood, Senior Customer Success Coach at Arena, led the webinar
We want to spend less time converting data into information and we want to spend more time making decisions that can lead to actions.
Phil Seymour, Director of Engineering Services at RAVE Aerospace
Audit complexity
Arena, a PTC company, helps organisations to change the world through innovative product use. It aims to unify product lifecycle management (PLM) and quality management system (QMS) processes. Through this, it aims to help teams work faster and more efficiently. In the webinar, Marshall speaks to Phil about how RAVE Aerospace is using a centralised PLM system to strengthen its operations.
RAVE Aerospace is a component manufacturing company, offering solutions across in-flight
entertainment
and connectivity. In order to provide an efficient and connected ecosystem, it uses modern consumer and avionics technology. The company partners with airlines and aircraft manufacturers to create a comfortable experience for passengers aboard flights.
RAVE has global operations, meaning it needs to adhere to each nations' legislation and expectations. To do so, RAVE uses a centralised PLM system, which allows it to maintain audit readiness,
improve visibility
, build trust in product data and develop stronger supplier relationships. In doing this, teams are able to maintain control, while also operating at a faster pace and undertaking a growth process.
For RAVE, the ability to stay audit-ready year-around is crucial. By using new technology, RAVE is able to link documents and approvals in one system. Through this, teams are demonstrating compliance at a record speed, without sacrificing standards when audits take place.
"Years ago, people would be shuffling through pieces of data, and people would be waiting for a simple answer," explains Phil.
Phil Seymour, Director of Engineering Services at RAVE Aerospace
"Now, with the central data base – that PLM with that source of truth in there – you can link pieces together. As we can connect it all together, it makes it very easy to approach audits."
Increasing decision-making capabilities
In the webinar, Phil and Marshall explore how RAVE is working with a single source of truth in order to eliminate fragmentation across operations and act with confidence when it comes to accurate decision-making.
ongoing automation
, the possibilities of acceleration seem endless. Hours of manual processes are removed from the workflow when teams implement automated tools. Digital workflows and electronic signatures aim to keep programs moving and reduce delays. As trade is so volatile in today's environment, having a streamlined operation is critical.
Technology helps reduce
wait-times dramatically, meaning processes can be taken to the next step faster.
"These tools, analytics and AI convert this raw data into real actionable information that you can take to decide what your next attack can be," Marshall explains.
PLM, ERP and other emerging tools all help teams spend less time gathering information. Through this, they can make informed decisions with greater confidence and speed.
"We want to spend less time converting data into information and we want to spend more time making decisions that can lead to actions," Phil says.
The webinar explores how RAVE Aerospace is taking modern problems and modern solutions in order to transform its operations. For supply chain leaders looking to modernise their supply chain and still remain in control, this session is not one to miss.

title: How Klaus Staubitzer Drives Digital Supply Chains at Siemens
content:
How Klaus Staubitzer Drives Digital Supply Chains at Siemens
Prioritise Us
on Google
Klaus Staubitzer, Chief Procurement Officer and Head of Supply Chain Management at Siemens. Credit: Klaus Staubitzer via LinkedIn
Klaus Staubitzer, CPO and Head of Supply Chain at Siemens has placed among the world’s supply chain leaders for driving resilience and sustainability
Klaus Staubitzer, CPO and Head of Supply Chain at Siemens, has placed 10th on Supply Chain Digital’s
Top 250 Supply Chain Leaders
For more than 30 years, Klaus has worked at Siemens, offering critical business insights in a range of leadership roles.
As a leader, he is working to better integrate sustainability and digitalisation within the supply chain and procurement ecosystem.
Leaders at the top of the list
Raj Subramaniam - CEO of FedEx
Tobias Meyer - CEO of DHL
Vincent Clerc - CEO of Maersk
Luc Reynaert - Chief Product Supply Officer at P&G
Chris Nielsen - EVP, CSCO, CQO at Toyota
Klaus’ career
Klaus has a rich history in procurement and cost savings, having studied Economics at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, followed by undertaking a PhD in Economics at the University of the Bundeswehr Munich.
In 1996, he joined Siemens as a Consultant for Strategic Procurement & Processes, a role which he held for two years.
Following this, he had a steady rise throughout the ranks. In 2001, he became CEO of the Business Segment at the company. In 2008, Klaus was named CPO & Head of Supply Chain, Sector Industry, which he held for five years.
His current role,
& Head of Supply Chain operates across all of Siemens AG. He has held this position for more than 13 years, leading teams through some of the most volatile periods in history.
Now, he oversees the Siemens Supply Chain, where he manages more than US$43bn in annual spend. Under his leadership, Siemens has seen significant transformation with digital integration and
sustainability initiatives
For SCM, sustainability and innovation are not just nice-to-haves. It would be very wrong to go back to relying on cost-cutting only.
Klaus Staubitzer, CPO and Head of Supply Chain at Siemens
Siemens is welcoming innovations like data centres while also supporting them. Credit: Siemens
The Siemens strategy
At Siemens, the real world is being combined with the digital one.
Industry, infrastructure
and transportation is being combined with software, data and AI. In the modern supply chain, technological adoption is crucial, helping organisations meet demands and gain greater visibility.
The global economy is changing, so Siemens is changing with it, adding new technologies such as automation, electrification and AI.  Its One Tech Strategy aims to provide faster and  more direct access to information in order to drive stronger customer focus and increased innovation across its portfolio.
“For me, AI and digitalisation are fundamentally a cultural transformation, not just a technical one,” Klaus explains on LinkedIn.
“When we stop seeing
AI as a threat
and start understanding it as a lever, I know it will be key to our value creation – and to better decisions, higher efficiency, and sustainable success.”
Under Klaus’ leadership, the Siemens supply chain is seeing significant growth across geography and digital markets. It is also building long-lasting and repeatable solutions to help across a range of industries including aerospace, life sciences, AI factories and rail transportation.
Digitalisation is a major part of that, helping unlock new value for customers by
expanding into new areas
and collaborating with the partner ecosystem at a much higher level.
Klaus has helped drive the One Tech strategy
Key companies
Microsoft
CEO: Satya Nadella
HQ: Washington, US
Microsoft and Siemens partnered to integrate Siemens Xcelerator with Microsoft Cloud, combining industrial automation with Azure's cloud computing power. Their collaboration focuses on AI-driven manufacturing, digital twins, and IoT solutions through Azure. They're jointly developing solutions for smart factories, predictive maintenance, and industrial metaverse applications. The partnership aims to accelerate digital transformation across manufacturing, infrastructure, and transportation sectors, making industrial operations more efficient and data-driven.
CEO: Jensen Huang
HQ: California, US
Siemens and NVIDIA collaborate on the industrial metaverse, integrating Siemens Xcelerator with NVIDIA Omniverse platform. This partnership enables photorealistic digital twins and AI-powered simulations for factory planning, robotics, and autonomous systems. They're developing solutions that allow engineers to design, simulate, and optimize industrial processes in virtual environments before physical implementation. The collaboration combines Siemens' industrial automation expertise with NVIDIA's GPU computing and AI capabilities.
CEO: Martin Sion
HQ: Saint-Ouen-sur-Seine, France
Siemens merged its rail mobility division (Siemens Mobility) with Alstom in 2021, though regulatory concerns blocked the full merger. They continue collaborating on railway projects, signaling systems, and rolling stock manufacturing. Both companies supply trains, rail infrastructure, and digital mobility solutions worldwide. They sometimes work as partners on major rail projects while competing in others. Their relationship involves technology sharing in areas like train control systems, electrification, and sustainable transportation solutions across European and global markets.

title: Amazon & Kuehne+Nagel: Developing a Long-Term Collaboration
content:
Amazon & Kuehne+Nagel: Developing a Long-Term Collaboration
Prioritise Us
on Google
Kuehne+Nagel has announced a strategic partnership with Amazon. Credit: Kuehne+Nagel
Stefan Paul, CEO of Kuehne+Nagel explores the long-term strategic collaboration with Amazon, as part of the logistics company’s strategic growth plan
Building on an existing relationship, Kuehne+Nagel has announced its long-term strategic collaboration with Amazon.
This is helping the organisation with its supply chain resilience and strategic growth plan, looking to further develop its logistics capabilities.
The partnership will make use of Amazon’s scale and
Kuehne+Nagel
’s history in transport and freight forwarding.
A history of growth
Kuehne+Nagel was formed as a freight forwarding company in Germany in 1890. In the last 130 years, it has grown into a global logistics partner, offering tailored solutions for major industries around the world.
The company operates out of more than 1,300 locations, connects 100 countries and is trusted by more than 400,000 customers.
As a company, it believes in being part of the bigger picture – using its thorough knowledge to develop a streamlined workflow between people and territories. Moreover, as a logistics company, it understands its responsibility to have a positive impact on the planet, and as such is working towards a
zero carbon future
Kuehne+Nagel collaborates closely with a range of organisations and industries, whether to integrate modern technology to its operations, implement sustainable logistics, or develop tailored solutions that ensure the growth of both the client and the
logistics organisation
Now, it has announced its long-term collaboration with Amazon.
We are excited to enter this long-term collaboration with Amazon, with a shared focus on scale, innovation and customer value
Stefan Paul, CEO of Kuehne+Nagel
Stefan Paul, CEO at Kuehne + Nagel
A look at the numbers
Kuehne+Nagel shares rose by more than 3% on the day of the announcement
Shares rose to a more-than 52-week high of CHF 228.40 (US$278.26)
K+N generated a net turnover of CHF 24.48bn (US$29.83bn) in FY25
More than 400,000 customers rely on K+N to manage their logistics
The AWS Cloud spans 124 Availability Zones
The partnership
Kuehne+Nagel is dedicated to its strategic growth initiatives, and its partnership with Amazon is part of that. The two companies already have an existing relationship, which means this growth in collaboration is reflective of their strong working capabilities.
With K+N’s global logistics capabilities, the partnership is designed to strengthen customer service
solutions for Amazon
and its other partners. The collaboration also includes Amazon Web Services (AWS), meaning the entire infrastructure lifecycle is included in this partnership.
The collaboration will oversee the construction and equipment deployment, as well well as ongoing maintenance, expansion projects and upgrades. Through this, each organisation will be encouraged to grow and modernise, with increasing global capabilities and logistics networks.
“We are excited to enter this long-term collaboration with Amazon, with a shared focus on scale, innovation and customer value,” explains Stefan Paul, CEO of Kuehne+Nagel.
“Kuehne+Nagel’s global network, digital capabilities and supply chain expertise are well positioned to support Amazon’s evolving business needs, enabling us to accelerate future growth opportunities and create lasting value for our customers. We are setting the foundation for a new level of customer service commitment at a global scale for Amazon.”
A significant part of the relationship will be the strengthening of supply chain resilience,
operational efficiency
and scalability for K+N.
According to K+N, this partnership could last up to seven years.
Kuehne+Nagel have a range of freight solutions to help support Amazon. Credit: Kuehne+Nagel
Key companies
CEO: Andy Jassy
HQ: Washington, USA
Amazon is a global e-commerce and technology giant founded in 1994, operating online marketplaces, retail platforms, and streaming services. Beyond retail, Amazon relies on complex logistics partnerships to manage worldwide fulfillment operations. The company works with freight forwarders like
Kuehne+Nagel
for international shipping and supply chain solutions, while its AWS division provides cloud infrastructure that powers digital transformation across logistics industries.
CEO: Matt Garman
HQ: Washington, USA
AWS is Amazon's cloud computing division, launched in 2006, offering infrastructure, platform, and software services globally. It's the world's leading cloud provider, serving businesses across industries. Kuehne+Nagel partners with AWS to digitize logistics operations, utilizing cloud technology for data analytics, supply chain visibility, and customer solutions. This collaboration enables K+N to modernize services and provide real-time tracking and optimization capabilities.
Kuehne+Nagel
CEO: Stefan Paul
HQ: Switzerland
Kuehne+Nagel is a Swiss-based global logistics company founded in 1890, specializing in sea freight, air freight, contract logistics, and overland operations. As a major freight forwarder, K+N handles shipments for numerous clients, including Amazon. The company leverages AWS cloud technology to enhance digital capabilities, improving supply chain efficiency and customer experience while potentially managing freight operations for Amazon's vast e-commerce network.

title: Why DHL is Strengthening Latin American Supply Chain
content:
Why DHL is Strengthening Latin American Supply Chain
Prioritise Us
on Google
DHL Supply Chain has entered into an agreement to acquire Open Market, a leading Colombian transport and logistics operator. Credit: Getty Images
Hendrik Venter, CEO of DHL Supply Chain, says acquiring Open Market will expand capabilities to support Strategy 2030 and healthcare logistics
DHL Supply Chain has entered into an agreement to acquire Open Market, a leading Colombian transport and logistics operator.
The strategic acquisition
advances DHL Group's Strategy
2030 by scaling its high-margin life sciences and healthcare footprint across Latin America.
Open Market contributes 21 warehouses, 13 cross-docking platforms, transportation capabilities and temperature-controlled operations.
Hendrik Venter, CEO of DHL Supply Chain, says: “This step reflects our strategic focus on strengthening our capabilities in regions and sectors that show sustained, long-term growth. Colombia's strong economic momentum and rising demand for integrated logistics and transport services make it a key growth market for DHL Group.”
DHL Acquires Open Market: Key Facts
Acquisition adds temperature-controlled transport and warehousing capabilities across Colombia
Deal supports DHL Group's Strategy 2030, focused on life sciences and healthcare growth
Open Market's infrastructure will integrate directly into DHL Supply Chain
Expansion builds on DHL's existing Constellation Distribution Centre hub near Bogotá
Around 4,100 Open Market employees will join the DHL Supply Chain workforce
Hendrik Venter, CEO of DHL Supply Chain
Increasing Colombian capabilities
Around 4,100 Open Market employees will join the DHL Supply Chain workforce, as the company says it is “better positioned to deliver reliable, customer-focused logistics solutions in the Colombian market”.
According to the
US International Trade
Administration, total bilateral trade in goods and services between the US and Colombia reached US$54.8bn in 2024.

title: Mercedes-Benz signs deal to put Wayve AI Driver in cars within 2 years
content:
Mercedes-Benz
autonomous driving
Fred Lambert
| Sep 22 2026 - 7:49 am PT
Mercedes-Benz has signed a definitive production agreement with British self-driving startup Wayve to build its “AI Driver” into future Mercedes vehicles, with integration starting within the next two years.
It’s the first time Wayve’s end-to-end driving AI is going into a production car in the premium segment, and it deepens a relationship that already includes Mercedes investing in Wayve’s $1.5 billion Series D round earlier this year.
What Mercedes is actually buying
Wayve doesn’t build cars. It builds the software that drives them, using what it calls an “AV2.0” approach: an embodied-AI system that learns to drive from data instead of following hand-coded rules and HD maps.
The company says its AI Driver runs without HD maps, geofences, or city-specific retraining, and can generalize to cities it hasn’t seen before. That’s the same “learned,” end-to-end philosophy Tesla uses for Full Self-Driving, and the opposite of the heavily mapped, geofenced approach Waymo built its robotaxis on.
However, unlike Tesla, which removed the radar from its sensor suite, Wayve added radar in its latest system.
Photo: Wayve
For this deal, Wayve integrated its AI Driver into Mercedes’ own production system architecture: the automaker’s hardware, its MB.OS operating system, and its map interfaces. The system was trained on Nvidia infrastructure running on Microsoft Azure. Mercedes describes what customers will get as “advanced urban and highway point-to-point driving assistance.”
And notice what the announcement leaves out. There’s no SAE automation level, no named models, and no firmer date than “within the next two years.”
“This partnership marks the world’s first integration of the Wayve AI Driver in the premium segment,” said Jörg Burzer, Mercedes-Benz’s chief technology officer.
Mercedes is now running three autonomy stacks
Mercedes isn’t betting on one self-driving system. It’s running several at once.
It already sells Drive Pilot, its own hands-off, eyes-off Level 3 system for highway traffic jams. That was the first Level 3 system certified for US roads. In January, we covered
Nvidia’s open-source Alpamayo model shipping in the Mercedes CLA
as a Level 2+ assistance system. Now Wayve’s AI Driver is coming too.
So Mercedes is hedging: a rules-based L3 system for a narrow highway case, Nvidia’s stack for L2+ point-to-point, and Wayve’s embodied AI as a scalable path toward higher automation. It’s the strategy of a company that wants autonomy, but it isn’t sure which path will suceed yet.
That’s the bigger story for the industry. While Tesla insists on writing every line of its self-driving software in-house, legacy automakers are increasingly buying the “AI driver” from specialists like Wayve, Nvidia, and Mobileye. Wayve now counts Mercedes, Nissan, and Stellantis among the investors in its
$1.5 billion Series D
, which valued the company at $8.6 billion in February.
“The pace and depth of our development work together reflect a deep technical alignment between our teams,” said Wayve co-founder and CEO Alex Kendall.
Electrek’s Take
I think it’s clear that other automakers will work with these ADAS/ADS system integrators rather than Tesla.
Not only do they avoid working with a competitor, but Tesla has also shown real difficulty maintaining FSD across several vehicle programs and different hardware versions (HW3). It would be hard for an automaker to trust Tesla with deploying and maintaining a system in other automakers’ vehicles.
Wayve’s entire business is built around that. It’s a way safer bet, especially with Mercedes’ ownership stake.

title: Tesla Full Self-Driving bug falsely flags dirty cameras, demands service
content:
Full Self-Driving (FSD)
Fred Lambert
| Sep 22 2026 - 7:26 am PT
Tesla’s newest Full Self-Driving update, v14.3.9, is telling owners their cameras are dirty when they aren’t — and sending them to service to fix a problem that doesn’t exist.
Tesla has confirmed the bug and is canceling the service appointments it triggered. A fix is expected in a coming update.
The alert owners are seeing
Drivers who installed v14.3.9 started getting a message on the center screen: “Poor camera visibility detected. Interior windshield residue cleaning is required.”
The cameras are clean. The alert fires anyway, often in bright sun or glare, with the software reading normal optical conditions as an obstructed forward camera.
Tesla owner
posted a screenshot of Tesla Support confirming the software fault and said Tesla is proactively canceling service visits that owners booked because of it. Owners on Reddit reported the same message on clean cars.
What triggered it, and what to do
v14.3.9 (software builds 2026.27.5 and 2026.27.6) rolled out around September 12. It’s the same update that brought
Automatic Collision Evasion to HW4 cars
, letting FSD take over manual driving to avoid a crash.
If you got the camera alert, don’t book a service appointment. Owners who already paid for a cleaning or inspection can contact Tesla Support for a refund.
A follow-up build, v14.3.10, is expected to address the alerts. So far, its release notes are identical to v14.3.9’s, so there’s no confirmation of what changed.
Electrek’s Take
Vision-only for the win. It’s a two-step forward, one-step back process.
The newest build is so twitchy about camera visibility that it’s flagging perfectly clean lenses and shipping owners off to service. It looks a lot like Tesla turned up the sensitivity on visibility detection and overshot.
A false “clean your camera” popup is an annoyance, not a danger. But it points at the real problem with a camera-only system: getting it to catch genuine degradation from sun, fog, and dust without crying wolf on a clean windshield is hard, and Tesla still hasn’t nailed it.
Tesla is likely to run into a thousand more of these issues before it can actually achive unsupervised self-driving at scale, which require redundancy – something you can’t achieve if your only way to see, cameras, fail.

title: BYD offers a closer look at the new Seagull EV [Images]
content:
Peter Johnson
| Sep 22 2026 - 7:12 am PT
revealed the second-generation Seagull design in a series of sketches: a bigger, smarter version of its most affordable EV.
When is BYD launching the new Seagull EV?
The Seagull, sold as the Dolphin Surf and Dolphin Mini in markets outside China, is BYD’s entry-level electric hatch.
In China, the Seagull starts at just 69,900 yuan, or about $10,000. That’s much cheaper than any new vehicle in the US. To give you a better idea, the
most affordable new car in the US
is the 2026 Hyundai Venue, which starts at just over $20,500.
Even in overseas markets, BYD’s electric hatch is among the most affordable EVs. In Europe, the Dolphin Surf starts at about €22,900 ($26,500).
It’s no wonder the low-cost electric hatch is among the world’s top-selling electric vehicles. According to Cleantechnica, the Seagull (including the Dolphin Surf and Mini) was the sixth best-selling EV globally through the first half of 2026, with over 27,500 units sold.
BYD is now preparing to launch the second-generation model. Zhang Zhuo, the general manager of BYD’s Ocean series sales division, offered a closer look at the new Seagull on Monday night.
Zhou revealed several design sketches of the updated version with the caption: “Preserving the classic design while embracing new expression, the lines have been reshaped and the surface refreshed #BYD Second Generation Seagull# More surprises are coming soon!”
When translated into English, the first image reads: “Brand new layout” and “Space size expands together.”
Another reads: “Clean appearance” and “The driving posture is even more extreme.” The other sketches reveal new “Trident-shaped” front and rear lights and the second-generation Seagull’s “Dynamic new look.”
No other details were mentioned, but Zhuo revealed at the Chengdu Auto Show last month that the new model will be named the “Great Seagull” and will go on sale by the end of 2026.
The new Seagull also appeared in China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) regulatory filing last month, revealing a few key specs.
The filing revealed that the Great Seagull measures 4,205 mm long, 1,810 mm wide, and 1,570 mm high, with a 2,650 mm wheelbase. That’s considerably bigger than the current Seagull, which is just 3,780 mm long.
It will also gain a more powerful 95 kW (127 hp) electric motor. In comparison, the current Seagull uses a 55 kW (75 hp) motor.
We will learn more soon, with its official debut just around the corner, but you can expect the updated version to feature BYD’s second-generation Blade Batteries and Flash Charging technology.
Earlier this week,
several spy images
of the new Seagull undisguised surfaced online, revealing a roof-mounted LiDAR. As such, the new version will likely get an upgraded ADAS system with BYD’s God’s Eye B.
We also caught a sneak peek of the interior last month with several updates, including a larger infotainment screen, redesigned center console, and a two-spoke steering wheel.
BYD Dolphin Surf EV (Source: BYD)
Will BYD release the second-gen model in overseas markets, like Europe and the UK? It hasn’t been confirmed, but the larger updated electric hatch is expected to launch overseas, likely as the second-gen Dolphin Surf.
The current Dolphin Surf starts at around €22,900 ($26,500) in Europe, so the larger variant will likely cost a bit more. It will likely still start at under €30,000 ($35,000), as a smaller, more affordable option than the Dolphin.

title: Waymo riders can now get $2.85 back when pairing a ride with public transit
content:
Robotaxi
Public Transit
Jameson Dow
| Sep 22 2026 - 7:00 am PT
Photo: Waymo
Waymo is now offering a $2.85 credit to any rider who pairs their ride with public transit, expanding a pilot program it previously ran in two cities – but it’s only available for Visa users, for now.
One of the great things about living in a city is that you can get around without a car. Higher housing density makes public transit possible, which then serves as a cheap way to move lots of people quickly.
But, every once in a while, you’ll still need some other solution to get where you’re going – especially in American cities where public transit
isn’t nearly as expansive as it ought to be
. Maybe you take a train into town because it’s cheaper and you can skip traffic, but the only stop is a couple miles from your destination.
For these situations, there are taxis. Instead of owning a car and finding a place to park it, you can just borrow a ride for a fee.
Of course in the modern age, we have robotaxis, driven by computers rather than humans, and Waymo is the leading provider of this service in the US.
So to assist with this symbiotic relationship between transit and taxis, Waymo is now offering a deal: anyone who takes a transit ride and a Waymo ride back to back gets a $2.85 reward back from Waymo.
The program is only available on Visa cards for the time being. Waymo would like to expand it to other payment processors, but has not yet done so. To use it, you link your Visa card to your Waymo app, and when you use the same card for both a Waymo and public transit ride within 2 hours of each other, you get $2.85 in “Waymo Cash,” which can be used for future Waymo rides.
Waymo initially ran a similar trial program in Los Angeles and San Francisco, and designed the program to mirror a
$2.85 discount
given to riders who use both BART and SF Muni, two regional transit systems, in the SF Bay Area.
The company says that in its most mature markets (SF/LA/Phoenix), over half of its riders also use public transit, so it expects to see high use of the
new program
. But the new program will be available initially to all riders in San Francisco, with the idea of expanding out from there.

title: Tesla's active robotaxi fleet in Austin crashes back to 8 vehicles after Cybercab pump
content:
Tesla’s active robotaxi fleet in Austin has fallen back to just 8 vehicles over the past seven days, according to data from community tracker Robotaxi Tracker.
That’s about the same number Tesla had on the road when it launched the service in June 2025. Fifteen months of promises, and no net growth. A surge following the “launch of the Cybercab” quickly dissipated.
Tesla’s “launch” spiked the numbers for about a week
Tesla held a Cybercab launch event in Austin on September 3 and invited a wave of supporters and Tesla influencers to ride the steering-wheel-free vehicle. For a few days, X was full of first-ride videos.
The tracker data shows exactly what that looked like. The number of unique Tesla robotaxis actually seen carrying riders in Austin spiked past 100 in early September, up from the 20-to-40 range it had been stuck in for most of the year.
Then it collapsed. By September 22, the seven-day active count is back to 8.
And the ride videos dried up with it. One of those early Cybercab rides turned a 10-minute trip into a 70-minute detour, and the flood of posts Tesla engineered for launch week has slowed to a trickle after Tesla “influencers” left the city.
Registered vehicles aren’t the same as active ones
Here’s the gap Tesla’s boosters keep glossing over.
Tesla registers its autonomous vehicles with the Texas DMV under the state’s new AV rules, and that registered fleet now sits at 476 VINs (409 Model Ys and 67 Cybercabs), up 285 in the last 30 days alone. TSLA pumpers point to that growing number, and to the rising Cybercab count in particular, as proof the fleet is scaling.
But a registration is a VIN in a database, not a car giving rides. Of those 476 registered vehicles, trackers have matched only 265 to license plates actually spotted on the road, and just 179 were seen at all in the last 30 days. Over the last 7 days, only 8 were caught carrying passengers.
Tesla keeps “adding” vehicles to its Texas robotaxi fleet on paper. That count has never reflected how many cars are actually operating at the same time.
Electrek’s Take
This is what a marketing launch looks like when there’s no product ramp behind it. And by product ramp, I mean useful Cybercabs. I do beleieve that Tesla can ramp up production and we have seen plenty of Cybercabs sitting in parking lots, but it currently has no way to translate that into autonomous ride-hailing at scale due to the same safety concerns we have been talking about for more than a year.
Top comment by Volvo Guy
What's interesting is that there is a spike about 2 weeks before the "launch" and then another spike at "launch". I'd bet good money that:
--The first spike was a test to make sure they were ready for the "launch" spike
--Both of these events are spikes rather than new plateaus because during both events, Tesla was remote monitoring every car and that is not sustainable. If they had truly autonomous operations, there would be no reason to scale back after ramping up. The cars would just keep running and the line would go up and to the right. The spike pattern demonstrates that these were tests, not actual scaling of ongoing operations
Tesla needed a moment, and it got one on September 3. It invited the usual crowd of supporters, and generated a week of glowing ride videos. The active-fleet chart shows the whole thing: a clean spike past 100 vehicles, then a cliff straight back down to 8. Once the influencers went home, so did the cars.
And 8 is rough. That’s essentially where the service started in June 2025. Fifteen months later, after a “launch,” a Cybercab reveal, and hundreds of new registrations, the number of Tesla robotaxis actually carrying people in Austin in a given week hasn’t moved.
That’s entirely because if Tesla deploys the system at scale, it would face too many accidents. Therefore, it is preferable to only run a few vehicles at a time, in geo-fenced areas, and at lower speeds.
There would be nothing wrong about that if Tesla wasn’t trying to convince the public, and mostly the stock market, that it is “leading the autonomous market with no close second behind” when in fact, it is mostly an act.

title: Honda just unveiled an electric mountain bike, and it looks serious
content:
Micah Toll
| Sep 22 2026 - 6:02 am PT
Honda is best known for motorcycles, cars, generators, lawnmowers, robots, jets… basically anything with a motor attached to it. But now the Japanese giant appears ready to add another two-wheeler to that list: an electric mountain bike.
Honda recently showed off its new e-MTB project at Sea Otter Europe in Girona, Spain, marking a surprisingly serious return to the mountain bike world after an absence of roughly two decades.
And this doesn’t appear to be merely a styling exercise. Honda’s German website is
already inviting
riders to register their interest in the upcoming e-MTB, declaring, “New terrain, same dream,” and describing the bike as “almost here.”
The prototype itself combines Honda’s
motorcycle-inspired design
with some decidedly familiar bicycle hardware. The carbon monocoque frame was developed with German premium e-bike manufacturer Rotwild through its ADP Engineering division, and features a massive rear swingarm that Honda calls the “Gullarm.”
The suspension uses a single-pivot arrangement with several linkages driving the rear shock, while a Fox 36 fork, mullet 29-inch front and 27.5-inch rear wheel setup, and aggressive geometry make it pretty clear Honda isn’t designing this thing for leisurely rides to the farmers market.
The display bike also uses a Shimano EP8-series mid-drive motor, though there may be another surprise lurking there. Footage
released
alongside the bike appears to show a slightly different motor casing than Shimano’s current EP801.
That’s hardly enough evidence to declare that a new Shimano motor is coming, but it certainly gives us something interesting to squint at until Honda provides more details.
Honda’s involvement in mountain biking actually goes back more than 20 years. Its motorcycle R&D division famously developed the RN01 downhill bike in the early 2000s, complete with an unusual enclosed, frame-mounted transmission. Honda raced the radical machine internationally before eventually pulling out of the sport.
That makes this return particularly interesting. Honda isn’t simply slapping its logo on a generic e-bike as many other automotive and motorcycle companies have done. The company even displayed the new machine alongside the old RN01 and its latest electric motorcycles and off-road prototypes.
Honda hasn’t announced the battery capacity, final motor, weight, price, production name, or launch markets yet.
But considering Honda is already collecting registrations for what it calls its “new E-Mountainbike,” this looks less like Honda wondering whether it should build an e-bike and more like the company preparing to actually sell one.

title: Massive UK study finds high-mileage electric cars more durable than petrol
content:
Electric Vehicles
reliability
Jameson Dow
| Sep 22 2026 - 5:00 am PT
A study of millions of UK vehicles shows that electric cars stay on the road longer than petrol cars, and the gap widens as mileage increases.
With electric cars being a
relatively
new technology, many people have been skeptical of what their long-term reliability would look like. Despite EVs having fewer moving parts which suggests less opportunity for failure, fear of the new still keeps people worrying.
But electric cars aren’t really
new anymore. The oldest EVs of the modern era have now been on the road for nearly two decades, so we’ve got some data now. And it turns out EVs look pretty good, according to a
new study
The study was conducted using
data from millions of annual British MOT tests
, the standard test of roadworthiness for cars on British roads. These tests focus on a car’s suspension, brakes, tires, exhaust, and emissions.
It checked how likely cars were to come back for another MOT test – if they didn’t, then that meant the car was no longer on the road (whether it be for an issue with those five categories above, or another issue).
In the beginning of their operational life, there’s little difference between roadworthiness of petrol and electric vehicles. EVs actually experience slightly
problems in the early years of ownership, but that’s because EVs tend to put on more miles early than petrol cars do.
When comparing on a mileage basis, EVs have very similar failure rates in the early years, differing by less than a percentage point. But that changes once you get to higher mileage numbers – past 40,000 miles lifetime.
At that point, petrol cars are less reliable, and the reliability only gets worse over time. By the time a petrol car reaches 120,000 miles, it’s
more likely to have failed than an EV (16% failure rate vs. 23.5% failure rate).
The same goes for age, as cars get older the EVs remain more reliable. That’s despite higher annual mileage from EVs no matter where they are in their age bracket.
The study also compared vehicles that have an electric and a petrol version side by side. In every case
the VW Golf, it was either a tie or a reliability win by BEVs.
This is despite the compromised BEV design of these multi-powertrain vehicles. Most of them were designed with limited chassis modifications, simply adding a large battery, making the BEV versions heavier than their chassis was designed for.
This weight discrepancy led to higher tire wear for BEVs. Across the board, BEVs did have significantly higher tire wear than petrol vehicles. But multi-powertrain vehicles like the VW Golf had much higher tire wear rates than purpose-built BEVs like the BMW i3.
While weight did have an effect on tire wear, it didn’t have an effect on suspension. The study found that BEVs suffered fewer suspension problems than petrol vehicles, no matter the mileage.
And brakes were obviously responsible for far fewer problems on BEVs, given that most braking happens via regenerative braking on electric cars. However, very old EVs (over 10 years old) ended up having more brake problems than petrol cars, likely due to persistent underuse of brakes and corrosion.
So, for EV drivers out there, be sure to hit those friction brakes every once in a while, EV drivers, even if you use regen most of the time. And keep an eye on your tires.
Not only is all of this true of light duty vehicles, but of light commercial vans like the Nissan NV200. The BEV version outperformed the diesel version, except on tire wear.
One limitation of the study is that it doesn’t track battery health, since that isn’t captured in British MOT tests. But we did recently see
the largest-ever study of battery health
that showed EV batteries last longer than many people would expect, generally retaining 90% of capacity even after 90,000 miles of operation.

title: Kenya backdates solar export charges by over a year - pv magazine Global
content:
Markets & Policy
Kenya’s energy regulator has codified charges for unauthorized solar exports and confirmed its net-metering credit rate – retroactive by more than a year, with no explanation given.
Brian Publicover
22 Sep 2026
Markets & Policy
Commercial & industrial
Kenya’s electricity regulator has formally codified charges for unauthorized solar power exports and confirmed net-metering credit provisions in a statement that takes retroactive legal effect more than a year before its publication date, with no public explanation given for the backdating.
Kenya backdated new solar-export rules by more than 14 months, and no one has explained why. The regulator’s changes, reported Sept. 21, are legally in effect retroactive to July 1, 2025 – but neither the government nor local media have said what’s behind the delayed disclosure.
The amendment introduces a formal definition of “dumping” – the unauthorized injection of electricity from a customer’s generation system into the Kenya Power and Lighting Co.’s (KPLC) network without company approval or a valid net-metering agreement. Energy dumped into the grid will be billed at the standard base tariff, and the Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA) or KPLC may pursue further action if the practice damages equipment, according to the notice.
The notice also codifies a net-metering export credit of 50% of a customer’s exported electricity, applied as a bill credit before pass-through costs, taxes and levies are calculated on total energy supplied. That rate is not new: it traces to Kenya’s Energy (Net-Metering) Regulations of 2024, which took effect in July of that year. The recent statement formalizes the existing rate within the tariff schedule rather than introducing a cut.
Net metering under the amended schedule remains capped at 1 MW of installed capacity per customer, also constrained by each customer’s maximum recorded demand over the prior 12 months. Commercial and industrial (C&I) customers seeking to self-consume solar power above that threshold must pursue separate embedded-generation or open-access arrangements rather than net metering.
Formal net-metering approval requires bidirectional metering and EPRA-licensed installation – conditions some industry observers say not all earlier installations meet, though no public estimates exist.
EPRA has not issued any enforcement notices or retroactive billing advisories under the new dumping definition. The Kenya Renewable Energy Association and solar installer organizations have also not made any public statement on either change.
The change comes as KPLC reported fiscal 2026 revenue up 8.6% to KES 238.24 billion ($1.8 billion) and profit up 2.1% to KES 24.99 billion for the year ended June. Management has cited the tariff structure as limiting revenue growth despite higher sales, though it hasn’t linked that constraint to the net-metering amendment.
Separately, the notice sets Kenya’s e-mobility tariff at KES 16 per unit for standard hours and KES 8 off-peak, removing a prior 15,000 kWh monthly cap that had constrained larger EV-charging operators. It gives no rationale for the change.
EPRA also confirmed three September pass-through charges – a KES 3.00 fuel energy cost charge, a KES 1.1443 foreign exchange adjustment, and a Water Resource Management Authority levy – adding KES 4.16 per unit to bills. All three are calculated before net-metering credits are applied, magnifying their impact on net-metered customers.
The 1 MW ceiling and the underlying net-metering framework aren’t new: EPRA first floated a
draft version of the rules in 2022
, capping eligible systems at the same 1 MW threshold and targeting roughly 100 MW of initial distributed solar deployment. What’s changed since is the retroactive codification of the export-credit rate and the new “dumping” penalty regime – additions that formalize enforcement around a policy Kenya has been building toward for four years.

title: EU prepares minimum energy-efficiency standards for data centers - pv magazine Global
content:
Markets & Policy
The European Commission has proposed a classification and labeling system for data centers and launched a consultation on minimum energy-efficiency standards. EU data center electricity consumption could rise from 68 TWh in 2024 to 114 TWh by 2030, driven largely by growing AI workloads.
Pilar Sánchez Molina
22 Sep 2026
Markets & Policy
Energy Storage
Utility-scale
The European Commission has presented a package of measures aimed at improving the energy efficiency of data centers and their integration into the European electricity system. The package includes a delegated regulation establishing a common classification and labeling system, alongside a public consultation on future minimum energy-performance standards.
The new classification system will apply to data centers with an installed IT power demand of more than 500 kW, allowing their energy and environmental performance to be compared. In addition to electricity consumption, the system will consider water use and indicators related to integration into the energy system, including clean energy generation, waste heat reuse and demand flexibility.
The Commission said data centers capable of adjusting their electricity consumption in response to grid conditions could help reduce system costs, improve grid stability and facilitate the integration of higher shares of renewable energy.
Waste heat reuse is another area under consideration. The Commission estimates that recovering around half of the waste heat generated by European data centers could provide enough heat to meet the needs of approximately 4 million households.
The delegated regulation is now subject to a two-month scrutiny period by the European Parliament and the Council. If neither raises objections, the regulation will enter into force, with the first sustainability labels for individual data centers expected in 2027. The Commission plans to review the classification system by the end of 2028.
In parallel, the Commission has launched a 12-week public consultation on potential minimum energy-efficiency requirements for data centers. Under the proposal, data centers would not be required to disclose their emissions or electricity and water consumption.
The consultation is open until Dec. 14, 2026, and its results will inform a legislative proposal expected in the second quarter of 2027.
The measures come amid rapid growth in Europe’s digital infrastructure. According to Commission data, data centers consumed around 68 TWh of electricity in the European Union in 2024. Consumption could rise to 114 TWh by 2030, driven largely by growing artificial intelligence workloads.
The European Union is also targeting a threefold increase in data center capacity
